facts: These are appeals by special leave granted against the judgment of a Single Judge of Bombay High Court in exercise of his jurisdiction u/s. 482 Criminal Procedure Code (hereinafter referred to as the Cr.P.C.') and Art.
The respondent had joined the police force as a P.S.I. Cadet on 1.June.1966 and after completion of his training, he was posted as Police Sub-Inspector in the Police force in 1968.

It appears that one A.C.P.R.B. Kolekar of Anti-corruption Bureau, Bombay on 1.January.1987 made enquiries with regard to the respondent who was, at that time, holding the post of Vigilance Officer in the office of the Transport Commissioner, Bombay.

A first information report was recorded by ACP Kolekar on 16.February.1988 and the case was registered vide C.R.No. 4/88 u/s. 5(2) read with S. 5(1) (e) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (hereinafter referred to as the Act).
The respondent then filed Criminal Writ Petition No. 854 of 1991 and the case was mentioned for admission before Mr. Justice M.F. Saldanha.

After the rule was issued, an affidavit in reply was filed and by the impugned judgment dated 16.October.1992, the proceedings, then pending before the Special Judge, Greater Bombay being Special Case No. 18/90 were quashed.
issues: Principles of natural justice had been denied and the provisions of the S. 5 of the Act had not been complied with because the respondent should have been given an opportunity of giving an explanation prior to the registration of the offence alleged against him

The Sanctioning Officer did not mention in the body of the Sanction Order that the property was disproportionate to his known sources of income and that the public servant could not satisfactorily account for the same
There had been a non-application of mind on the part of the sanctioning authority
petitioner_arguments: The learned Single Judge ought not to have interfered with the prosecution, once it had been launched
It would have been open to the respondent herein to raise any contention which he wanted before the Special Judge
In support of his contention, learned counsel has relied on the following decisions, namely; K.Veeraswami Vs. Union of India and others, (1991)3 SCC 655 1991 Indlaw SC 711
respondent_arguments: The respondent would be unduly and unnecessarily narassed if he was required to take part in a protracted trial

There were serious allegations of mala fides against the authorities and principles of natural justice were violated because no opportunity was granted to the respondent before the First Information Report was filed
court_reasoning: In our opinion there was no warrant for the High Court coming to the said conclusion and the judgment has to be set-aside

A party to the proceedings cannot be allowed, at this stage at least to take a chance and if he gets the impression that he will not succeed to seek permission to withdraw the original proceedings obviously with a view to regitate the same contentions, which have been or may be, adjudicated upon, by a higher court before the subordinate court though in different proceedings
holding: The judgment has to be set-aside
There was no warrant for the High Court coming to the said conclusion
